title: Vasquez requires such to-be-remitted faith; most Romans deny particular remitted/to-be-remitted as faith object
source_text: LVII. Qualem etiam fidem ad justificationem necessariam esse expresse docet Vasquez locis ante citatis, & de tali fide putat exponendum ipsius Concilii Tridentini Canonem, ubi agitur de fide per quam justificamur. Veruntamen plerique Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae misericordiam specialem quoquomodo consideratam negant esse fidei objectum, hoc est, negant fidei proprium actum esse ut credamus nobis in particulari peccata vel remissa, vel certo remittenda esse.
pass_a_gloss: Vasquez also expressly teaches that such faith is necessary for justification in the places cited before, and thinks the Canon of the Council of Trent itself, where faith by which we are justified is treated, is to be expounded of such faith. Nevertheless most Doctors of the Roman Church deny that special mercy however considered is an object of faith — that is, they deny that it is a proper act of faith that we believe sins in particular are either remitted to us or certainly to be remitted.
pass_b_english: Vasquez requires that to-be-remitted faith for justification and reads Trent justifying-faith Canon of it.
Most Roman doctors still deny special mercy however taken as faith object — denying particular remitted or certainly-to-be-remitted belief as faith proper act.

choices.why: Vasquez vs majority Rome on particular mercy as faith-act.
